one_line_contribution: The claim is that an item-level partition of memory-free failures into coverage failures (gold never sampled in n draws) versus selection failures (gold sampled but outvoted) predicts a mechanism-level division of labour — injected experience can only convert coverage failures, instruction optimization only selection failures, and injection damage lands on high-agreement solved items — plus the control that follows from it (agreement-gated memory vs. agreement-gated extra plain sampling at matched tokens, E3-i/P4) and the stratum-decomposed disjointness test between GEPA-style instruction search and a self-editing bank (E7/P6).
closest_prior_work: The proposal concedes MemRL, MemDelta, Evo-Memory, 2511.04234 and the Adaptive-Consistency line, but it never names the work that actually threatens the surviving contribution: the coverage-vs-selection partition IS the pass@k-minus-maj@k decomposition, introduced and named as coverage versus verification/selection in Brown et al., 'Large Language Monkeys: Scaling Inference Compute with Repeated Sampling' (2024), and used throughout the repeated-sampling and verifier-selection literature (Chen et al. 'Are More LLM Calls All You Need?'; the pass@k-vs-pass@1 RLVR debate; verifier-free best-of-n work). The 'recoverable-coverage ceiling' is oracle-gated pass@k analysis with a new name. What is genuinely unclaimed by that line is only the *attribution* use — bucketing an intervention's fixes and breaks by the sampler's coverage/selection stratum — which is a modest analytic move, not a new object. E3-i (AGS) is likewise the natural application of Adaptive-Consistency's own control to a memory arm; MemRL already puts Pass@k sampling beside memory under one protocol, which is most of P1. Novelty therefore rests on the E7 disjointness test, and that test as specified is not decisive (see strongest_objection).
strongest_objection: P6, the only prediction carrying the track's headline coupling question, cannot fail in its stated form. Jaccard overlap < 0.25 between INSTR's and MEM's fixed-item sets is what two *independent* interventions produce by chance: the pilot reports GEPA fixing roughly as many items as it breaks (order tens of items) and the motivating anomaly reports the bank fixing zero and breaking six to seven, so the two fix sets will be small sets drawn from ~200-300 wrong items, and their expected chance Jaccard is well under 0.10. The proposal states no permutation/chance-overlap null conditioned on each mechanism's marginal fix count and per-item difficulty, so 'disjoint' will be declared whether or not the mechanisms are actually complementary. The same defect sinks P2's first clause: '≥60% of memory's fixes fall in COVERAGE-FAIL' is a share, not a rate, and is uninformative without the stratum base rates — if COVERAGE-FAIL is 15% of items and SELECTION-FAIL is 10%, a proportional, mechanism-free scatter of fixes already clears 60%. The prediction that tests the mechanism is fix *rate per stratum* (fixes / stratum size), and it is not the one pre-registered. Compounding this, all of E7 and P2's fix-side analysis has an empty-denominator risk the power section never addresses: the 800-item, 3.1-point MDE is computed for a global accuracy contrast, while P6 and P2 are statements about the composition of maybe 10-30 fixed items per arm. If the pilot's 'fixed zero items' replicates, memory's fix set is empty and P2/P6/P4's 'advantage concentrated in COVERAGE-FAIL' are undefined rather than refuted, and the paper is left with the bounded null plus E0's ceiling — i.e. one more compute-matched replication of MemRL/MemDelta on a smaller model.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Re-pre-register P6 as an overlap odds ratio against a permutation null that fixes each mechanism's marginal fix count and strata/difficulty, with a stated MDE for that statistic, and re-pre-register P2 as per-stratum fix and break *rates* with confidence intervals rather than shares of a total. (2) State the minimum fix count under which E7 and P2 are declared uninformative-by-design, and add a pre-committed fallback (e.g. pooling INSTR fixes across strata, or raising the optimizer budget) so the arm cannot silently return an undefined answer. (3) Show that the stratum labels are stable, not an artifact of n=8: pool A's 24 rollouts permit a re-label at n=16 or n=24; report the COVERAGE-FAIL churn rate between disjoint 8-draws and the fraction of n=8 COVERAGE-FAIL items covered at n=24, since any item with small nonzero gold mass is relabelled by resampling alone and will be 'fixed' by any perturbation, memory or not. (4) Add the extra-retrieval control named below, without which P4 does not license the sentence in the title. (5) Say explicitly whether E6's online reflector sees gold answers or correctness feedback when writing entries from held-out rollouts; if it does, the online arm is transductive label leakage across the 800 evaluation items and its ceiling gain in P7 is not comparable to the static bank, and if it does not, the write path differs from the static bank's and confounds contrast (a). (6) Decompose P7, which is currently a four-way conjunction with no stated reading for partial outcomes.
missing_baseline: Agreement-gated *extra retrieval* — spending the gated token budget on more search calls, more retrieved passages, or an extra hop rather than on injected experience or on extra samples. In multi-hop QA over a local Wikipedia index, a coverage failure is overwhelmingly a case where the supporting passage never entered the context, so the direct competitor to 'inject distilled experience on low-agreement items' is 'retrieve more documents on low-agreement items' at the same cost. The plan's AGS controls only for extra sampling, so a P4 win would leave the reviewer's obvious alternative explanation — memory is a slow proxy for retrieval depth — untested, and Adaptive-RAG (dropped as 'redundant with the confidence gate') was exactly that control. Secondary omission: a content-matched but irrelevant injection arm at held-out (k tokens of random or off-task bank entries), which is the only way to separate the pilot's own finding that *volume*, not content, was the causal lever from the claim that experience content does the work; the k-sweep varies volume while holding content relevant and cannot make that separation.
preprint_collision: The check reports that the search tool hit a hard usage limit and returned nothing this round, and the authors correctly refuse to read that silence as novelty — the honesty is creditable but it does not substitute for the search. As submitted, the novelty claim is explicitly self-labelled 'unverified as of now' and rests on a carried-over search of unstated date, so by the standard that an unsearched novelty claim is a weakness, this is a weakness and not a neutral. Beyond the missing round, the carried-over check has a substantive blind spot: none of its queries ('compute-matched agent memory', 'self-consistency vs experience retrieval', 'when does retrieved experience hurt', 'coverage vs selection failure sampling', 'prompt optimization and memory division of labour') would surface the repeated-sampling literature where the coverage/selection split originates (Large Language Monkeys and its successors), and no such work is cited anywhere in the proposal — so the one contribution the authors say survives has not been searched for under its established name. The committed pre-submission search must add queries for pass@k vs maj@k, coverage vs verification gap, and sample-selection bottleneck, and must check for 2026 preprints attributing agent-memory gains to sample-selection versus generation, which is the live area most likely to hold a direct collision.
